title: I Own It. But Can I Prove It? How a Laptop Sale Took Me to the Police Station
excerpt: I knew the laptop was mine. I had bought it, repaired it, used it for years, and eventually decided to sell it. But when someone claimed it was their stolen laptop and the police became involved, I discovered an uncomfortable truth: owning something and proving you own it are two different things. Here's what happened and what I learned.
content:
I Own It. But Can I Prove It?
The laptop was mine. I knew it was mine. The problem was proving it.
Most of us don't think much about proving that we own the used things we own.
You buy a used laptop. You use it for years. You repair it. You take photographs of it. Eventually, you decide to sell it.
Why would you need anything more?
I didn't think I needed anything more either.
Then, in August 2026, I found myself sitting at a police station trying to prove that a laptop I was selling actually belonged to me.
And that experience changed how I think about ownership.
